title: A month with Sarah Vaughan in Los Angeles
summary: Monk briefly played with Sarah Vaughan but would not give up electric bass.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: But I couldn't stop, I couldn't give up on it. I really couldn't give up on it. I left town a couple times, went to Los Angeles because I wasn't getting any playing, I wasn't able to play. I couldn't get it out or any kind of way. , and I went down...I took a job in Los Angeles. And while I was there I got a call with Sarah Vaughan. I played with Sarah about a month. It only lasted that long, and I couldn't understand why Sarah would call me, because I know electric bass with Sarah Vaughan just didn't go together.

And I wasn't going to give up the electric bass for the upright, for Sarah or nobody else. I knew what I wanted to do, but because of her husband at that time...We were very tight, and a family thing there and...I guess they just kind of experimented with it. Which is OK with me, because I love Sarah, and musically too. But that period didn't last long.

And of all things, I was in Los Angeles just catching jobs and, whatever it was, and I couldn't get my mind off of, you know, that. I couldn't put my whole mind on seriously anything but coming back to Las Vegas. And here I was, in that short period of time, how do I get back there and do what I want to do? And that was most important in my mind, some way.
